description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian dish featuring succulent chicken pieces simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Its mild spice and sweet notes make it a favorite for all ages, perfect for a comforting and flavorful lunch or dinner. This recipe guides you to create an authentic restaurant-quality experience right in your home.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook in batches until browned and lightly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add whole green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Simmer the Sauce
instructions.text: Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste to the pan and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the tomato puree, soaked cashews, sugar, and salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the whole spices (cardamoms, cinnamon stick, bay leaf). Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. If needed, add a splash of water to achieve desired consistency. Pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra smooth texture.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth sauce. Stir well and simmer for another 5-7 minutes to allow the chicken to absorb the flavors and cook through completely. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed kasoori methi. Heat through gently without boiling. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.

tips: For a deeper flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer the marination, the more tender and flavorful your chicken will be.
Do not skip straining the sauce after blending. This step is crucial for achieving the signature silky-smooth texture of authentic Murgh Makhani.
Always add cream and kasoori methi at the very end and avoid vigorous boiling afterward to prevent the cream from splitting and to preserve the delicate aroma of the fenugreek.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Guide to a Beloved Indian Lunch Recipe

There are few dishes in Indian cuisine that evoke such widespread delight and comfort as Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, with its luscious, creamy tomato-based gravy and tender pieces of chicken, has captivated palates worldwide. Perfect for a hearty Indian lunch, Butter Chicken offers a symphony of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, making it an irresistible choice for any occasion. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a kitchen novice, mastering this classic recipe will bring the warmth and richness of India right to your dining table.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the 1950s in Delhi, India, specifically to the Moti Mahal restaurant. Legend has it that the chefs at Moti Mahal experimented with leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was a culinary masterpiece that quickly gained international fame.

At its core, Butter Chicken is characterized by marinated chicken (often grilled or pan-fried) swimming in a velvety smooth gravy. The gravy is a complex blend of tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a medley of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and coriander. What truly sets it apart is the generous addition of butter and cream, which impart an unparalleled richness and silky texture. A crucial ingredient for its authentic flavor profile is kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), which adds a distinct, slightly bitter, and earthy aroma. This dish is celebrated for its mild heat, making it accessible to those who prefer less spice, while still delivering an explosion of flavor. It’s the ultimate comfort food, deeply satisfying and wonderfully indulgent, making it a stellar choice among Indian lunch recipes.

## Ingredients You Need

To create an authentic Butter Chicken, you’ll need a combination of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, optional but recommended for smoothness)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, to balance acidity)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (plus extra for garnish)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh coriander leaves, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making delicious Butter Chicken at home is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a perfect result:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, flipping occasionally, until browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes (or tomato puree), soaked cashews, turmeric powder, red chili powder, ground coriander, and ground cumin. Mix well and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sides.

5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully transfer the tomato-cashew mixture to a blender. Add about 1/2 cup of water and blend until extremely smooth. For an extra silky texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.

6.  **Simmer the Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, garam masala, and crushed kasuri methi. Stir to combine. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich sauce. If the gravy is too thick, add a splash of water.

7.  **Finish with Cream and Sugar:** Stir in the heavy cream and sugar. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, just until heated through. Do not boil vigorously after adding the cream, as it can curdle. Taste and adjust salt and sugar as needed.

8.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish your incredible Butter Chicken with a swirl of extra cream and fresh chopped coriander leaves.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is easier with a few expert tricks:

*   **Marination Time is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal if you have the time.
*   **Don't Skip the Cashews:** Cashews are crucial for the gravy's characteristic creaminess and body. If you don't have cashews, almonds can be a decent substitute, but cashews provide a more authentic flavor.
*   **Blend Until Super Smooth:** For a truly silky gravy, blend the tomato-cashew mixture thoroughly. Passing it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending will ensure there are no gritty bits, resulting in a luxurious texture.
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder:** For that vibrant red color without excessive heat, opt for Kashmiri red chili powder. If unavailable, use a mix of regular red chili powder and a pinch of paprika.
*   **Roast Kasuri Methi:** Briefly toast the kasuri methi in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing it. This intensifies its aroma and flavor significantly.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Butter Chicken is all about balance. The sugar helps cut through the acidity of the tomatoes, while the cream and butter add richness. Adjust these to your personal preference.
*   **Good Quality Butter and Cream:** Since these are star ingredients, using high-quality unsalted butter and full-fat heavy cream will make a noticeable difference in the final taste and texture of your homemade Butter Chicken.

## Serving Suggestions

Your delicious Butter Chicken deserves equally delightful accompaniments. Here are some classic serving suggestions:

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, chewy naan bread is the quintessential pairing. Its ability to soak up the rich gravy is unmatched. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly good choices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Fluffy basmati rice, or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice), provides a subtle base that perfectly complements the robust flavors of the Murgh Makhani.
*   **Roti or Chapati:** For a lighter option, whole wheat roti or chapati also pairs wonderfully with the creamy gravy.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple side salad of sliced cucumbers, tomatoes, and onions with a squeeze of lemon juice can add a refreshing contrast to the richness of the dish.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based raita (like cucumber raita) can help balance the flavors and provide a pleasant counterpoint.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is a beloved masterpiece, don't hesitate to experiment with variations to suit your dietary needs or preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** For a meat-free version, replace the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, chickpeas, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and potatoes. Simply pan-fry your chosen substitute and add it to the gravy as you would the chicken.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** For a dairy-free take, use coconut cream or full-fat coconut milk instead of heavy cream, and a plant-based butter alternative. While the flavor profile will shift slightly, it can still be incredibly delicious.
*   **Spiciness Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to control the heat. For more spice, add a finely chopped green chili to the gravy base. For milder flavor, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you want a restaurant-style smoky flavor, try the "dhungar" method. Heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot, place it in a small bowl inside the cooked curry, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over it, and quickly cover the pot for a few minutes.
*   **Different Chicken Cuts:** While boneless thighs are recommended for their tenderness, you can use bone-in chicken pieces for a more rustic flavor, just ensure they are fully cooked.

Indulging in a bowl of homemade Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is an experience in itself. Its rich history, complex flavors, and comforting warmth make it a truly special Indian lunch recipe. With this comprehensive guide, you’re well-equipped to recreate this iconic dish in your own kitchen and savor every spoonful. Enjoy the culinary journey!
